title: A Harsh Answer Splits the Kingdom
overview: Solomon's son Rehoboam refuses to ease his people's burdens, and the northern tribes break away from David's family for good.

parts.label: A plea at Shechem (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: The tribes gather at Shechem, an old northern meeting place, to make Rehoboam king, and Jeroboam comes back from Egypt, where he had fled from Solomon. Their request is simple: ease the forced labor and heavy demands of Solomon's reign, and we will serve you.

parts.label: Two sets of advisers (vv. 6-11)
parts.note: The older men who served Solomon tell him that a little kindness now will win the people's loyalty for good. His young friends tell him to boast that his little finger is thicker than his father's waist and to threaten 'scorpions,' probably a more brutal kind of whip, though the exact meaning is uncertain.

parts.label: The harsh reply (vv. 12-15)
parts.note: Rehoboam follows his friends and answers with threats. The writer says God was behind this turn of events, fulfilling the prophet Ahijah's earlier message that most tribes would be taken from Solomon's line, yet Rehoboam's arrogance still comes across as his own foolish choice.

parts.label: The north walks away (vv. 16-19)
parts.note: 'To your tents' is a call to go home and owe David's family nothing, leaving Rehoboam to rule only the people living in Judah. When he sends the very official in charge of forced labor, the crowd stones him to death, and the split between northern Israel and southern Judah becomes permanent.

disagreement: Christians differ over verse 15, some reading it as God directly causing Rehoboam's stubbornness and others as God allowing a freely made foolish choice and working through it.
think: When someone with power over you chose to act tough rather than listen, what do you think was really driving that choice?
